text:
Anya: Anyone seeing the eu-west GPU-provision job blocked? CI terraform apply #458 hung during an import with a state lock error.
Mike: I see the same. Argo infra-reconciler started a sync at ~08:12 which overlaps the CI apply.
Jamal: log snippet: ```Error: Error locking state: ConditionalCheckFailedException: The conditional request failed\n2026-03-11T08:12:34Z [INFO] attempting import: module.gpu.aws_autoscaling_group.pool``` - stuck during import step.
Kai: This smells like a workspace alias rename + GitOps reconcile racing the branch CI apply. Two terraform applies hitting the same state key.
Anya: Can we safely unblock the pipeline? GPU pool scaling is blocked and customers are seeing queueing.
Mike: Pause the Argo app for that infra stack first (I've put it into "paused" sync). Then check the lock table to get the lock id.
Jamal: Found lock row in dynamodb `redwood-tfstate-locks` for key `eu-west/gpu-pool` with lock_id `a1b2c3d4-9f00-11ec-0a1b-0c9d8e7f6a5b` and timestamp older than 12m.
Kai: That lock appears stale (the CI job that created it died). From the ci-ops bastion I ran: `terraform force-unlock a1b2c3d4-9f00-11ec-0a1b-0c9d8e7f6a5b` and re-ran the import apply in interactive mode.
Anya: Is force-unlock safe here? worried about concurrent state corruption.
Mike: It's safe only because we paused Argo and confirmed no active apply (check `ps` on the runner and cloudwatch logs). Always fetch the lock timestamp and runner job id first.
Jamal: After force-unlock I did a targeted apply: `terraform apply -target=module.gpu -auto-approve` from the dedicated ops runner. Import completed.
Anya: We still have a stray state alias `workspace_alias:gpu-pool-v2` pointing to a half-imported resource. How did that happen?
Mike: I ran `terraform state list` and found duplicate entries. Did `terraform state rm module.gpu.duplicate_alias` then `terraform import module.gpu.aws_autoscaling_group.pool <asg-id>` in the same apply. Verified `terraform state list` shows only the expected resources.
Kai: Follow-ups: added a short CI gate that fails if a dynamodb lock exists for that key and patched our GitOps ArgoCD app to add an annotation `infrastructure.redwood/hold-sync: "true"` while CI runs to avoid future races. Also filed INFRA-834 to add a pre-sync lock-check hook.
InfraBot: Incident recorded: INF-2026-03-gitops-lock (tagged eng-infra, ops-oncall)
Anya: Thanks folks — GPU pool scale-up completed and queues cleared. Can someone paste these recovery steps into the infra runbook?
Kai: Will do. Also recommending we bump lock TTL / add better lock detection in the gitops operator. :thumbsup:
Mike: quick note for runbook: 1) pause Argo app 2) verify no active runner 3) read lock_id from dynamodb 4) terraform force-unlock LOCK_ID 5) targeted apply/import 6) remove stray state entries if any 7) resume Argo sync.
Anya: Perfect, closing this thread."
